payload.boundary: INSIDE: engine/worktree.ts (provisioning, shipMerge, retire), the close path in engine/loop.ts that calls it, engine/gate.ts where a bless is recorded (the commit trigger and the pointer triple), and the grant record's shape. OUTSIDE, with its interface named: git itself (the merge, index, tag and tree-read commands - SE speaks to it only through engine/git.ts's allowlisted spawn); engine/project.ts and the board (they READ what the close leaves behind - the interface is the on-disk live claims plus the grant index, and rewiring them to git is i5e); the systematic machine (it decides WHEN a close happens, not how); the file lane and every other tool (they already resolve to the iteration's root and do not change here); the owner (holds the push, always).
payload.intended_use: An iteration runs in its own worktree on its own branch. Each time a gate is blessed, SE commits that milestone to the branch, so the work is durable and the tree is clean. When the iteration closes, SE tags the branch, then merges it into trunk in such a way that the merge commit keeps both parents while its tree carries only the live claims. Trunk gains the design nodes, requirements, tests and product code. The evidence, gate records and machine state remain on the branch under the tag, reachable by name and absent from any checkout of trunk. If anything about that sequence cannot be completed - the branch has no commits, the tag cannot be created, the merge conflicts - the close refuses and changes nothing.
payload.excluded_use: Binding does-NOT-do list for this iteration. It does NOT read anything back from git - no board, projectState or tooling change to resolve archived content (i5e). It does NOT touch the existing iterations already on disk - no backport, no deletion, no migration (i5e). It does NOT change the top-level machine, its states, or how iterations are presented (i11). It does NOT change any board panel (i9). It does NOT move grants.jsonl off trunk - the owner ruled it stays as a thin index. It does NOT rewrite history: no rebase, no force-push, no amending published commits; superseded content that lives only in history must survive. It does NOT push. It does NOT change what a gate, a bless or an evidence document MEANS - only where the resulting files live. It does NOT introduce parallel execution of iterations.
